title: R 4.6.0 macOS arm64 install URL returns 404
description:
Hi! Just ran into this on CI today and figured I'd flag it.

The arm64 URL the API returns for R 4.6.0 is dead:

```bash
$ curl -s "https://api.r-hub.io/rversions/resolve/4.6.0/macos/arm64"
# returns: https://cran.rstudio.com/bin/macosx/big-sur-arm64/base/R-4.6.0-arm64.pkg

$ curl -sI "https://cran.rstudio.com/bin/macosx/big-sur-arm64/base/R-4.6.0-arm64.pkg"
HTTP/2 404
```

Looks like CRAN moved the arm64 binaries to a new location with 4.6.0. The package now lives at `sonoma-arm64/` and that one works:

```bash
$ curl -sI "https://cran.rstudio.com/bin/macosx/sonoma-arm64/base/R-4.6.0-arm64.pkg"
HTTP/2 200
```

The CRAN page (https://cran.r-project.org/bin/macosx/) confirms it — they bumped the arm64 minimum from Big Sur to Sonoma for 4.6.0, and `big-sur-arm64/base/` still ends at R-4.5.3.

A side effect of this is that `release/macos/arm64` now returns 4.5.3 instead of 4.6.0:

```bash
$ curl -s "https://api.r-hub.io/rversions/resolve/release/macos/arm64"
# returns version 4.5.3

$ curl -s "https://api.r-hub.io/rversions/resolve/release/macos"
# returns version 4.6.0 (Intel)
```

Where this bit me: I'm using `r-lib/actions/setup-r@v2` with `r-version: release` on `macos-latest`. It just installs whatever URL the API gives it, so my macOS runner has been silently on R 4.5.3 since 4.6.0 came out, while Linux and Windows are on 4.6.0. Took a while to figure out what was going on because `setup-r` doesn't say anything — the OS is just \"release\" and there's no warning that the actual installed version differs from what the other runners get. Pinning `r-version: 4.6.0` would just turn the silent fallback into a hard 404, which I guess at least would've made it more obvious.

If it helps for the fix, this looks like the same shape of bug as #35 from the 4.3.0 release — probably just needs the arm64 path mapping to know about `sonoma-arm64/` for R ≥ 4.6.0.

Thanks for maintaining this!

title: Rtools query in scope?
description:
I see that we can query the `Rtools` versions from the API directly:

https://api.r-hub.io/rversions

Would it be in-scope to surface those in this package somewhere? Or should we just ping the REST API if we need that?

title: Estimated SVN revision number for release?
description:
AIUI r-core does a lot of cherry-picking to include/exclude certain features, so we (probably) can't say "Version 3.6.3 was precisely r8xxxx", but it may still be worthwhile to associate each release with a ~rough revision number.

Maybe the SVN revision at the timestamp in `r_versions()` would be a good enough proxy (as long as it's well-documented that this is more heuristic than canon)?

title: r_release_macos() returning R 4.2.3 instead of current version 4.3.0
description:
According to https://cran.r-project.org, the current release version for both Apple silicon (M1/M2) and Intel (x86) processors is 4.3.0, released 21 April 2023. As of this date (14 June 2023), `rversions::r_release_macos()` returns 4.2.3 as the current version.

Output from `r_release()` and `r_release_macos()`:

```
> rversions::r_release()

    version                date         nickname
131   4.3.0 2023-04-21 07:06:14 Already Tomorrow

> rversions::r_release_macos()

    version                date                                                    URL

130   4.2.3 2023-03-15 08:06:01 https://cran.r-project.org/bin/macosx/base/R-4.2.3.pkg
            nickname
130 Shortstop Beagle
```

This appears to be because the directory [https://cran.r-project.org/bin/macosx/base/](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/macosx/base/), which I believe `rversions::r_release_macos()` is checking, now contains legacy releases for pre-macOS X 11.0 versions of the OS, which have not been updated. Releases for the current version of R for macOS are now found in [https://cran.r-project.org/bin/macosx/big-sur-arm64/base/](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/macosx/big-sur-arm64/base/).

```
> packageVersion("rversions")
[1] ‘2.1.2’
```

title: Latest R version 4.0.3 seems not stable and giving unnecessary errors.
description:
I just updated my R base yesterday and stated working on `plm` package. When I was running the `random` effects model in R, I found an unexpected error that number of variables are more than estimable. The exact error was:

`Error in swar_Between_check(estm[[2]], method) :    model not estimable as there are 8 coefficient(s) (incl. intercept) to be estimated for the between model but only 6 individual(s)
 `

For the time being, i ignored that assuming that it must be an issue with `plm` package. But, later, I asked someone else to update R to `4.0.3` version and was told that this error is occurring there too, which was working fine earlier in older version. 

I confirmed that this error is not because of `plm` package when `lm()` also gave same type of error: of more variables than estimable.

I was running only 6 variables. Although, it should not matter since there is no limit on number of variables in calculating models through these functions.

title: unable to convert R versions data frame to tibble
description:
I tried to convert the data frame returned by `r_versions()` to a `tibble` but got an error message about the `date` column being of `POSIXlt` which is not supported by `dplyr` (see tidyverse/dplyr#179)

I found a workaround as per my repex below, but I was wondering what is the rationale to store the release date as `POSIXlt` (introduced as fix for r-hub/rversions#13) rather than `POSIXct` (which would make it ok for `dplyr`)...

Here is my rexex for this issue:

``` r
# remotes::install_github("r-hub/rversions")
library(rversions)
library(dplyr)
#> Warning: package 'dplyr' was built under R version 3.6.1
#> 
#> Attaching package: 'dplyr'
#> The following objects are masked from 'package:stats':
#> 
#>     filter, lag
#> The following objects are masked from 'package:base':
#> 
#>     intersect, setdiff, setequal, union

# fails
r_versions() %>% as_tibble()
#> Column `date` is a date/time and must be stored as POSIXct, not POSIXlt.

# fails too, for context see https://github.com/tidyverse/dplyr/issues/179 
r_versions() %>%
  mutate(date = as.character(date)) %>% 
  mutate(date = lubridate::as_datetime(date))
#> Column `date` is a date/time and must be stored as POSIXct, not POSIXlt.

# workaround: convert Posixlt column to char/datetime
vers <- r_versions()
vers$date <- as.character(vers$date) %>%
  lubridate::as_datetime()

# success
vers %>% as_tibble()
#> # A tibble: 114 x 3
#>    version date                nickname
#>    <chr>   <dttm>              <chr>   
#>  1 0.60    1997-12-04 08:47:58 <NA>    
#>  2 0.61    1997-12-21 13:09:22 <NA>    
#>  3 0.61.1  1998-01-10 00:31:55 <NA>    
#>  4 0.61.2  1998-03-14 19:25:55 <NA>    
#>  5 0.61.3  1998-05-02 07:58:17 <NA>    
#>  6 0.62    1998-06-14 12:56:20 <NA>    
#>  7 0.62.1  1998-06-14 22:13:25 <NA>    
#>  8 0.62.2  1998-07-10 11:13:45 <NA>    
#>  9 0.62.3  1998-08-28 09:02:19 <NA>    
#> 10 0.62.4  1998-10-23 12:08:41 <NA>    
#> # ... with 104 more rows
```
